Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight exists through the Court of Administrative Justice, which has handled cases related to national ID issuance (e.g., ordering the Civil Status Department to issue IDs to Baha'i families in 2006). The Economic Court of Alexandria issued a landmark data protection judgment (Feb 2025, EGP 10 million award vs Orange Egypt for SIM data breach). Data protection enforcement under PDPL is via both the PDPC and civil courts. The proposed Criminal Procedure Code (2025) adds judicial approval requirement for communications surveillance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by independent corroboration. HRW and EIPR both document that the Cairo Court of Administrative Justice ruled repeatedly on ID-related cases (2006-2008 Baha'i identity-document litigation), and Shehata & Partners confirms the Feb 2025 Alexandria Economic Court data-protection judgment (EGP 10m vs Orange Egypt). This is general judicial review of administrative/civil matters rather than an ID-specific statutory appeal mechanism, so code 2 is retained.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: The national ID system is directly linked to civil registration. The 14-digit national number is assigned at birth registration and remains linked to the individual for life. The Civil Registry Authority (under Ministry of Interior) manages both birth/death/marriage registration and national ID issuance. The Department of Civil Registration was established in 1960; computerized ID introduced in 1995. Smart civil registry machines also dispense birth certificates using national ID authentication. The Unified National Registry (UNR) cross-references civil registration data.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. CITC (the Civil Status Information Center, an official Egyptian government technical body) confirms the national ID database is technically integrated with birth, death, marriage, divorce and family-registration databases as well as numerous external agencies (Ministry of Justice, Social Solidarity, Central Bank, etc.), all under the single national-number system assigned at birth. This is closer to full integration than partial, so the code is raised to 3.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: PDPL No. 151/2020 requires explicit consent for data processing and sharing; cross-border data transfer requires PDPC approval. Banking Law No. 194/2020 restricts sharing of customer financial data with foreign entities. Telecommunications Law restricts transfer of telecom-related data outside Egypt. The NTRA IoT framework requires institutional/technical measures to protect user data. Executive regulations issued December 2025 provide detailed data sharing rules. The framework is established but enforcement is still maturing.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. Multiple independent law-firm sources (CMS, ELDIB, Shalakany) confirm the PDPL Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decision 816/2025) were issued 1 Nov 2025, published in the Official Gazette, and made publicly available in Dec 2025, with detailed rules on collection, storage, sharing, biometric data, CCTV and cross-border transfer. The chambers.com source cited originally is now dead (page removed). Given the rules are now published and public, code raised to 3 (fully available), though a national-security carve-out (Article 3) limits scope and enforcement only begins Nov 2026 — noted for awareness.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Egypt has a comprehensive legal framework: Civil Status Law No. 143/1994 mandates the national ID system; Personal Data Protection Law No. 151/2020 governs data protection with executive regulations issued in December 2025; FRA Fintech Law No. 5/2022 and Decrees 139-141/2023 cover digital ID for financial services; Cybercrime Law No. 175/2018; Telecommunications Law No. 10/2003; Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2002; 2014 Constitution guarantees privacy. Multiple sector-specific laws complement the foundational framework.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The Civil Registry Authority under the Ministry of Interior is responsible for maintenance and management of the national ID system. The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) oversees the Haweya digital ID platform for financial services. NTRA maintains telecom-linked identity aspects. The system is government-owned and government-maintained with no evidence of significant private sector co-management of the foundational ID system.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with fuller evidence. CITC (an Egyptian state technical body) runs day-to-day operation of the core national-number database in-country, but the French vendor IDEMIA has held recurring contracts for biometric device production (with local partner AOI) and competed for a EUR100m banking-security contract, showing continued foreign-vendor dependence for biometric hardware/technology alongside domestic operational capacity. This mixed picture supports 'partial in-country capacity' (2).

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The national ID system is funded through government budget (Ministry of Interior) supplemented by tiered user fees (50 EGP standard to 800 EGP immediate issuance). Digital transformation is supported by the Egypt Vision 2030 strategy and Digital Egypt 2026 initiative, with significant ICT sector investment (digital exports reached $7.4 billion in FY2024). The Haweya platform is backed by the CBE and private sector (Raya IT). Long-term sustainability appears ensured through both state commitment and revenue generation, though detailed public financial data on ID system budgets is not published.

revision_notes: Not confirmed either way. The Instagram source cannot be verified and is dropped. The see.news article corroborates state budget commitment and ICT-sector growth but says nothing about ID-system financing specifically, and no World Bank or donor loan tied directly to the core national ID system (as opposed to the separate, IBRD-financed Takaful and Karama social registry) could be found. Original code 2 is left unchanged but flagged for human review given the weak evidentiary base on both sides.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The national ID card includes a personal photograph. Fingerprint-based authentication is used at civil registry self-service machines for document retrieval, and facial recognition is used in the MOIEG-PASS biometric app (pilot 2026) and the Haweya platform (face + fingerprint). The physical card itself does not carry a biometric chip. FRA Decree No. 140/2023 mandates biometrics (facial + fingerprint) for fintech digital ID processes. Biometrics are collected at enrollment in these digital systems but the base card does not embed them.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The Civil Registry Authority maintains a centralized electronic database covering the full Egyptian population. Each citizen has a unique 14-digit national number assigned by the civil registry computer at birth registration. The back of the ID card contains an encrypted PDF417 optical code. The Unified National Registry (UNR) cross-checks data across government programs. Smart civil registry machines with touch screens and biometric authentication are deployed in major malls and operate 24/7.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Egypt has a mandatory national ID card (Betaqa/Identity Verification Card) computerized since 1995, governed by Civil Status Law No. 143/1994. The Civil Registry Authority under the Ministry of Interior manages the system. A digital overlay (MOIEG-PASS for government portal auth) was piloted in Feb 2026 and the Haweya digital ID platform announced in late 2025 for financial services. The foundational ID is well-established and digital; however, it lacks a chip/biometric passport layer.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The foundational Betaqa card is fully deployed nationwide and has been for decades, but the modern digital-identity authentication layer (Egypt Pass/di.gov.eg single sign-on, MOIEG-PASS facial-recognition app, Haweya) is still in pilot/roll-out phase as of early-mid 2026, per Ahram Online and the official di.gov.eg site. Code 4 (Partially deployed) is retained as the best fit for this mixed maturity.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National ID is mandatory for all banking transactions in Egypt. Bank account opening requires national ID per CBE and AML Law requirements. Egypt's financial inclusion rate reached 76% by mid-2024, with 53 million adults having bank accounts. The Haweya digital ID platform (CBE) enables remote bank account opening for 37 banks using digital ID. Mobile wallet registration (NTRA rules) requires valid national ID number. The ID is pervasively used across the financial sector.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Biometric Update confirms Haweya's 37-bank eKYC rollout and the 76% financial-inclusion figure; NTRA's own mobile-wallet page confirms ID-linked registration requirements. Code 3 (Mandatory) stands.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: The Egyptian national ID card is recognized within Arab League countries for travel and identity verification purposes. Egypt is a member of the Arab League and its national ID is accepted for entry in several Arab states (Jordan, Libya, etc.) under bilateral agreements. However, Egypt does not have a biometric e-passport, which limits cross-border digital recognition. The UNDP framework (Jan 2026) for Arab States specifically targets interoperability of digital IDs across the region but implementation is nascent.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Unconfirmed as stated; likely overstated but not clearly wrong. Regulaforensics does not in fact discuss cross-border recognition. The strongest evidence found is the Egypt-Sudan Four Freedoms Agreement, which allows movement on a 'passport or other document agreed by the two parties' — a plausible but not explicit basis for ID-card-only travel. Most Egyptian cross-border travel evidence found relates to the passport, not the national ID card, and the cited UNDP framework is prospective, not current. Code 2 is left unchanged as plausible but flagged for human review given weak direct evidence for the ID-card claim specifically.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: National ID is required for enrollment in the Universal Health Insurance System (UHIS). By June 2024, over 3.13 million were enrolled representing 81% of the population in the 4 Phase 1 governorates. More than 66% of Egyptians were covered by public health insurance programs in 2023. The eHealth Egypt project and National Health Information Infrastructure (NHII) use patient identification linked to national ID. The ID is used but a nationwide integrated digital health ID system is still being implemented.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The World Bank/P4H policy note (Feb 2025) verifies UHIS enrollment linked to national ID via the Unified National Registry, with UHIS still rolling out by governorate (i.e. not yet nationwide or mandatory). Code 2 (Accepted but not mandatory) stands.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Non-nationals (foreign residents) are required to register with GAPIN (General Administration of Passports, Immigration and Nationality) and obtain a residence permit card (separate from the Egyptian national ID). All foreign nationals must be registered with GAPIN and hold an ID card to maintain access to government services. The residence permit card serves as their official ID in Egypt. SIM card purchase is also available to foreigners using their passport and residency documents.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refined. UNHCR Egypt and the AIDA/ECRE 2025 country report confirm refugees/asylum seekers register with UNHCR first, then obtain GAPIN residence permits, and that Law No. 164/2024 now creates a distinct statutory 'refugee identity document' regime separate from the citizen national ID. This is consistent with 'Some' (2), i.e. eligibility exists via a separate, conditional pathway rather than full equivalence with citizens.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Egypt's population is approximately 107 million (2024). The national ID is mandatory for all citizens 15+. Egypt introduced computerized IDs in 1995 and as of 2007-2008 required all citizens to transition to computerized cards. Coverage is high given the mandatory nature and widespread use for employment, banking, voting, healthcare. However, precise enrollment percentage is not officially published. Given that ID is required for virtually all formal economic/civil activities and the system has been in place for 30 years, coverage is estimated at 85-95% of eligible population.

Comments: SIM card registration mandatorily requires the original national ID card for Egyptians (NTRA regulations). The sales agent keeps a copy of the national ID. Each Egyptian can register up to 10 voice lines and 5 data lines per operator using their national ID number. Foreigners must use passport and residency documents. NTRA also mandated IMEI registration via its Digital Service Platform from January 2025. The national ID is integral and mandatory for all SIM purchases.
